EQUITY ALERT: Rosen Law Firm Files Securities Class Action Lawsuit on Behalf of MNTN, Inc. Investors – MNTN

Rosen Law Firm, a global investor rights law firm, announces it has filed a class action lawsuit on behalf of purchasers of the securities of MNTN, Inc. (NYSE: MNTN) between August 5, 2026 and November 4, 2026, both dates inclusive (the “Class Period”). The lawsuit seeks to recover damages for MNTN, Inc. investors under the federal securities laws.

To join the MNTN, Inc. class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/mntn-inc/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action.

According to the lawsuit, defendants made false and/or misleading statements and/or failed to disclose that: (1) Defendants materially overstated MNTN, Inc.’s business prospects, considering that MNTN, Inc. had instituted changes that caused many experienced salespeople to leave MNTN, Inc.; (2) the foregoing materially impacted MNTN, Inc.’s ability to meet its previously issued guidance for 2026; and (3) as a result, defendants' statements about MNTN Inc.’s business, operations, and prospects were materially false and misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times. When the true details entered the market, the lawsuit claims that investors suffered damages.

A class action lawsuit has already been filed. If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you must move the Court no later than January 19, 2027. data.title: fraud0 Partners with FouAnalytics to Offer Impression-Level Digital Media Governance - to Replace DoubleVerify and IAS
data.description:
fraud0 Partners with FouAnalytics to Offer Impression-Level Digital Media Governance - to Replace DoubleVerify and IAS

fraud0 Partners with FouAnalytics to Offer Impression-Level Digital Media Governance - to Replace DoubleVerify and IAS

PR Newswire

NEW YORK and MUNICH, Nov. 20, 2026

Advertisers get every impression measured by FouAnalytics, humans and bots both counted, and wasted spend recovered through fraud0 Google Ads refunds

NEW YORK and MUNICH , Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- fraud0, the company behind the AI agent for Google Ads refunds, today announced a further partnership with FouAnalytics, the independent analytics platform for digital ads, websites and mobile apps. This partnership builds on the companies' earlier agreement to offer Google Ads refunds to advertisers. It lets fraud0 customers use FouAnalytics impression-level measurement as their digital media governance system, replacing legacy verification vendors such as DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science (IAS).

For more than a decade, legacy verification reports have told advertisers that invalid traffic (IVT) was around 1% and that their campaigns were 99% "fraud free." Independent audits have consistently found much higher levels of fraud and waste. Today, even advertisers no longer believe these low IVT numbers from the legacy vendors, and many are looking for an independent way to see what is really happening in their campaigns.

FouAnalytics was built to give them that view. It measures every ad impression and collects 300 to 500 parameters for each one. The platform is deterministic, not probabilistic. It uses red flags to mark automation and blue flags to mark real human interaction, such as mouse movements, scrolling and touch events. Because it positively measures for humans, not just bots, advertisers have two levers to pull. They can cut off sources of fraud (less red, bots) and shift budget toward sites and apps that reach more real people (more blue, humans). FouAnalytics also detects other forms of waste, like ad stacking, pixel stuffing, made-for-advertising (MFA) sites, ad slot refreshing and forced redirects.

FouAnalytics in-ad tags fire after the ad has rendered, so they record where the ad actually ran, not just what the bid request claimed. This matters because fraudulent sites routinely put reputable domains in their bid requests to win bids. Log-level data repeats those false domains, which lets fraud and MFA sites disappear from reports. FouAnalytics impression-level data shows where the ads really went. Advertisers can then compare bids won, ads served and ads actually rendered.

The FouAnalytics dashboard summarizes and labels impression-level data so executives can act on it quickly, without needing data scientists to process billions of rows of log files. If a third of impressions in a month are marked dark red, advertisers know right away which bad sites and apps to add to block lists. Setup takes minutes -- advertisers just copy and paste FouAnalytics in-ad tags into their DSP or ad server.

FouAnalytics also has cybersecurity built in. Every tag is unique and single-use, and its code is obfuscated, so bad actors can't tamper with measurement or test their bots against detection. The platform is privacy-compliant by design. It never collects personally identifiable information, never sets cookies, and keeps EU data in its Frankfurt data center, and IP addresses are discarded.

The partnership gives advertisers a complete governance loop. FouAnalytics shows them, impression by impression, where their money went and whether real humans saw their ads. fraud0 then analyzes invalid clicks, bots, billing anomalies, overdelivery and traffic outside targeted regions, then builds the evidence and manages refund claims with Google. Approved refunds are credited back to the advertiser's Google Ads account.

"Legacy verification was designed to reassure advertisers, not to protect them," said Dr. Augustine Fou, founder and CEO of FouAnalytics. "FouAnalytics measures every impression so advertisers can 'see Fou themselves' where their ads went and whether humans saw them. Paired with fraud0's refund capabilities, advertisers can now find the waste and get the money back. That is real governance, not transparency theater."

"We see far too many bot clicks in display campaigns,just like with other types of campaigns," said Tilman Pfeiffer, CEO of fraud0. "Now we can finally give our customers the placement-level data to identify and remove this wasted spend"

Advertisers interested in replacing legacy verification with impression-level governance and automated Google Ads refunds can contact fraud0 or FouAnalytics.

About fraud0
fraud0 is a leading bot detection and invalid traffic (IVT) prevention platform, trusted by some of Europe's largest banks, insurance companies, e-commerce businesses, and leading brands. Its privacy-friendly technology helps companies eliminate fraudulent traffic, protect ad spend, and improve marketing performance. More details at www.fraud0.com.

About FouAnalytics
Created by Dr. Augustine Fou, FouAnalytics is the most trusted, and the only truly independent analytics platform for digital ads, websites, and mobile apps. The platform provides detailed analytical data so practitioners can "see Fou themselves"™ why something is "high humanness," and troubleshoot what is not good quality. Today FouAnalytics is used globally by advertisers like Microsoft, Inuvo, Viant, Beiersdorf and Georgia Pacific, independent agencies and every agency holding company on behalf of clients, as well as more than 10,000 SMBs and site owners. More details at www.fouanalytics.com.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Belgium's Credit Rating, Warns of High Debt Levels
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Fitch Ratings affirmed Belgium's credit rating and outlook while warning that the country's strengths are somewhat offset by its high levels of debt and political environment.

The credit ratings firm assigned Belgium an A+ sovereign debt rating and a stable outlook due to its diversified and wealthy economy, as well as its membership in the eurozone.

Belgium's public debt is rising and is among the highest in the A rating category, Fitch said. Debt is set to be nearly 110% of gross domestic product by the end of this year, compared with the A rating average of 60%.

The nation's deficit is expected to start rising again in 2029 due to income tax reduction and a further rise in debt interest expenses.

Belgium's structural reforms implemented this year and last should contain social spending, Fitch said. However, fiscal pressure from rising costs persist and the reform measures have sparked protests.

Growth in the country was weaker in the first half of this year than expected, causing Fitch to lower its growth forecast for the year to 0.7%. Private consumption has suffered from higher energy prices, while exports are starting to recover after years of underperformance.

data.title: TechCreate Group Ltd. Provides Update on NYSE American Delisting Proceedings
data.description:
TechCreate Group Ltd. Provides Update on NYSE American Delisting Proceedings

TechCreate Group Ltd. (OTCMKTS: TCGLF) (“TechCreate” or the “Company”), a technology consultancy and advanced software solutions provider specializing in payment solutions, cybersecurity, and digital services, announced that the NYSE American Committee for Review (the “Committee”) has unanimously determined to affirm the decision of the NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) Listing Qualifications Panel (the “Panel”) with respect to the delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. Following its review, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) has determined not to pursue any further challenge to the Committee’s decision.

The Committee’s written decision, dated November 9, 2026, follows a hearing held on October 22, 2026 and affirms the Panel’s August 20, 2026 opinion, which upheld the NYSE American Staff (“Staff”) determination to commence delisting proceedings. The proceedings stem from the one-day trading suspension of the Company’s securities ordered by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) and effective on February 2, 2026, the stated basis for which was potential manipulation of the Company’s securities through social media recommendations made by unknown persons.

In reaching its determination, the Board reviewed the sequence of the appeal proceedings and the Committee’s written decision, and considered the following:

  • No finding of wrongdoing. The Committee’s decision states that the Staff’s investigation into the manipulative trading of the Company’s securities did not result in a finding of wrongdoing on the part of the Company or any of its officers and directors.
  • Exchange discretion. The Committee determined that the NYSE American Company Guide (the “Company Guide”) gives the Staff discretion to delist a security regardless of whether the issuer complies with applicable listing standards. The Committee acknowledged the preventive measures the Company put forward, including voluntary surveillance, reporting and escalation procedures, and enhanced Board oversight, but did not consider them sufficient to continue the listing.
  • Focus on the business. The Board believes the Company’s time and resources are better directed to operating and growing the business, and to evaluating alternatives intended to protect the interests of shareholders.

Under Section 1206 of the Company Guide, the Committee’s decision may be called for review by the Exchange’s Board of Directors at the request of one or more of its directors. If the decision is not called for review, the Company will be notified that it represents the final action of the Exchange. If the decision is not called for review and the Company receives such notice, the Exchange is expected to proceed with delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. The Company’s securities continue to be quoted in the over-the-counter market under the symbol TCGLF.

About TechCreate Group Ltd.

TechCreate Group Ltd. is a Singapore-based payment software solutions provider. Founded in 2015, the Company delivers digital payment and infrastructure solutions to financial institutions, telecommunications companies, deposit insurers and enterprises. TechCreate’s offerings include real-time payment systems, digital banking platforms, API management, cybersecurity and cloud computing. Its proprietary Artificial Intelligence Real-Time Engine (AI-RTE) is designed to enable fast, secure and efficient payment processing. For more information, visit https://www.techcreate.com.sg/.

APPLIED AEROSPACE & DEFENSE, INC. INVESTIGATION: AADX Securities Investors Encouraged to Contact Kirby McInerney LLP About Their Rights

The law firm of Kirby McInerney LLP is investigating potential claims against Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. (“Applied” or the “Company”) (NYSE: AADX). The investigation concerns whether the Company and/or members of its senior management may have violated federal securities laws or engaged in other unlawful business practices. If you purchased or otherwise acquired Applied securities, please contact Lauren Molinaro of Kirby McInerney LLP by email at investigations@kmllp.com, or fill out the contact form below, to learn more about your rights.

[LEARN MORE ABOUT POTENTIAL SECURITIES FRAUD CLAIMS]

What Happened?

On June 2, 2026, Applied priced its initial public offering of 32.5 million shares at $20.00 per share and began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on June 3, 2026. Then, on November 11, 2026, Applied reported its third quarter 2026 financial results and lowered its full year 2026 guidance, now expecting total revenue of between $660 million and $670 million, down from $670 million to $690 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $137 million to $142 million, down from $150 million to $155 million. The Company stated that it was “addressing equipment commissioning delays, supplier constraints and productivity issues in parts of our established operations. Together, those factors are affecting the efficient use of our resources in the near term.” Furthermore, the Company revealed that “approval and supplier issues are expected to move between $15 million and $20 million of rotorcraft aftermarket revenue from the fourth quarter into the first half of 2027.” On this news, the price of Applied shares declined by $1.42 per share, or approximately 13.2%, from $10.72 per share on November 9, 2026 to close at $9.30 on November 11, 2026.

What Should I Do?

At this stage, no lawsuit has been filed. The investigation is ongoing to determine whether claims may be brought under federal securities laws.

If you purchased or otherwise acquired Applied securities, have information, or would like to learn more about this investigation, please contact Lauren Molinaro of Kirby McInerney LLP by email at investigations@kmllp.com, or fill out the contact form below, to discuss your rights or interests with respect to these matters at no cost.

data.title: Surgery Partners, Inc. Announces Expiration and Results of Consent Solicitation Relating to Surgery Center Holdings, Inc.’s 7.250% Senior Notes due 2032

BRENTWOOD, Tenn., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Surgery Partners, Inc. (“Surgery Partners”) (Nasdaq: SGRY) announced today the results of the previously announced solicitation of consents (the “Consent Solicitation”) by its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Surgery Center Holdings, Inc. (the “Issuer”), from holders (“Holders”) of its outstanding $1,225,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.250% Senior Notes due 2032 (CUSIP Nos. 86881W AF9 / U86786 AD9 / U86786 AE7; ISINs US86881WAF95 / USU86786AD98 / USU86786AE71) (the “Notes”) to certain proposed amendments (the “Proposed Amendments”) to the indenture governing the Notes, dated as of April 10, 2024 (as supplemented, the “Indenture”), among the Issuer, the guarantors party thereto and Wilmington Trust, National Association, as trustee (the “Trustee”). The Consent Solicitation was made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Issuer’s Consent Solicitation Statement, dated November 16, 2026 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated November 16, 2026, and Amendment No. 2 thereto, dated November 18, 2026, the “Consent Solicitation Statement”).

The Consent Solicitation expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 20, 2026 (the “Expiration Time”). As of the Expiration Time, according to information provided by S&P Global Inc., the information and tabulation agent for the Consent Solicitation, the Issuer had received the requisite consents with respect to the Notes (the “Requisite Consents”) to effect the Proposed Amendments.

As previously announced, on October 23, 2026, Surgery Partners entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated as of November 8, 2026, and as it may be further amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”) with Spyglass Topco, LLC (“Topco”), Spyglass Merger Subsidiary, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (“Merger Sub”), and, solely for the limited purposes set forth therein, Bon Secours Mercy Health, Inc. (“BSMH”). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Surgery Partners, with Surgery Partners surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (the “Merger”).

The Proposed Amendments will amend the Indenture to (i) provide that, concurrently with and following the consummation of the Merger in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date (as defined in the Merger Agreement), each of BSMH, HealthSpan Partners, a 501(c)(3) Ohio corporation affiliated with BSMH, and their respective affiliates, and certain groups of which any of them are members, will be “Permitted Holders” under the Indenture, in addition to the existing Permitted Holders, and (ii) add to, amend, supplement or change certain other defined terms in the Indenture related to the foregoing. Except for the Proposed Amendments, all existing terms of the Notes and the Indenture will remain unchanged, and the Proposed Amendments will not alter the Issuer’s obligation to pay the principal of or interest on the Notes or the stated interest rate or maturity date of the Notes.

The Issuer intends to execute a supplemental indenture to the Indenture setting forth the Proposed Amendments (the “Supplemental Indenture”) on or around November 24, 2026. The Supplemental Indenture will become effective upon its execution and delivery, but the Proposed Amendments will become operative only immediately prior to the consummation of the Merger, provided that the Consent Fee has been paid. Once operative, the Proposed Amendments will be binding on all Holders, including those that did not deliver consents. If the Consent Fee is paid but the Merger is not consummated on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date, the Proposed Amendments will not become operative, and Holders that received the Consent Fee will retain it.

Holders who validly delivered (and did not validly revoke) consents prior to the Expiration Time will receive a cash payment equal to $5.00 per $1,000 in principal amount of Notes for which such consents were delivered (the “Consent Fee”). The Issuer expects to pay the Consent Fee on November 24, 2026, whether or not the Merger is consummated.

Jefferies LLC acted as solicitation agent and S&P Global Inc. acted as information and tabulation agent in connection with the Consent Solicitation. Questions regarding the Consent Solicitation may be directed to Jefferies LLC at (212) 284-2368 (collect) or to S&P Global Inc. at (212) 849-3880 (banks and brokers) or (888) 593-9546 (toll-free), or by email at consentoffer@spglobal.com.

data.title: Financials Down on Anthropic Fears — Financials Roundup
data.description:
Shares of banks and other financial institutions fell amid fears that the Anthropic IPO was the last hurrah for the Wall Street artificial-intelligence bonanza.

Global lender Citigroup underestimated the size of assets at a U.K. unit by $35 billion after mistakes in how it counted trades.

U.K. digital lender OakNorth, backed by a consortium including Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners firm, secured a U.S. banking license to expand its commercial lending operations.
